purpose: Literal source provenance and bounded interpretation; this authored index is not primary evidence.

source_reconciliation.policy: Preserve all exact 43 seeded source objects and all three products; the raw duplicate differs only in assignment agency and date. No source narrowing or biological NEW import is needed.

source_access.scope: Selected genuine normal abstract is unchanged. Original full PMC Methods/Results/Discussion were recovered externally and read; the independent consultation additionally inspected the original S7 simultaneous-binding experiment. Human constructs, rat rSly1 and endogenous human association are distinguished.
source_access.finding: COG4 brings the COG complex into contact with SCFD1/Sly1 and has a separate STX5-binding surface. Purified human COG4 (1–231) binds rat rSly1; endogenous HeLa assays support the human association. Binding-selective mutants distinguish recruitment from complex incorporation and link the activity to retrograde trafficking.

source_access.scope: The selected exact-main cache is a complete abstract. Original author-uploaded indexed full Methods, Table I and Results were read externally; all constructs are human. No source-cache replacement was made.
source_access.finding: Human COG4 forms positive contacts with COG1, COG2, COG5 and COG7 in reticulocyte-lysate co-translation/co-immunoprecipitation; the assembly analysis supports its scaffold role. Direct binary affinity was not measured with purified proteins.

source_access.scope: Actual selected full Methods/Results, assay descriptions and figure legends were read. No additional image-pixel or all-subunit-equivalence claim is made.
source_access.finding: Human HEK293T COG4 knockout alters Golgi ultrastructure, subunit stability and glycan processing. Replacement COG4 localizes to the Golgi and reverses glycosylation defects. Pathway-level toxin assays support retrograde traffic while receptor-binding changes limit some probes.

source_access.scope: The selected exact-main cache contains an abstract and limited body sections. Those actual passages and exact interaction records were read. A genuine fuller fresh normal variant is archived separately and is not substituted or described as the selected cache.
source_access.finding: BioPlex detects COG4 associations with four COG subunits and MUL1 by AP-MS. Exact records preserve assay hosts, tags and partner identities; co-purification does not require a purified direct interface.

source_access.scope: Selected full Results/Discussion and assay-validation legends were read, with exact 42-field target/paper/partner records. No separate full Methods access is claimed from this cache.
source_access.finding: HuRI supplies positive binary interaction records for COG4 (253–785) and eight exact partner products. The records include validated two-hybrid detections; orthogonal validation reported for the dataset is not automatically assigned to each target pair.

source_access.scope: Selected full AP-MS Methods and acquisition Results were read. The original linked NDEx network was authenticated from its prior genuine download and the exact accession-matched edge inspected.
source_access.finding: The original U2OS AP-MS network contains a COG2-bait/COG4-prey edge, supporting the source-specific association. The multimodal cell map is not itself evidence for every inferred function of the pair.

source_access.scope: Complete selected normal abstract read. The original full article was not recovered or inspected.
source_access.finding: The yeast Sec34/35 tethering complex and structural relationships to other tethering complexes provide evolutionary context. This abstract does not independently establish a human COG4-specific catalytic activity.

source_access.scope: Actual selected full patient/fractionation/transport Methods, Results and Discussion were read. Variant coordinates are those reported in this original paper.
source_access.finding: Patient fibroblasts with p.R729W and a deletion have reduced COG4, altered Golgi architecture and delayed retrograde trafficking, yet retain complex formation. Fractionation supports a major cytosolic subcomplex pool and a membrane-associated pool. Overexpression also perturbs trafficking, complicating rescue.

source_access.scope: Complete selected normal abstract read, plus original PubMed figure legends. Full Methods/Results recovery attempts did not succeed; no full-body access is claimed.
source_access.finding: A human COG4 C-terminal structure and HeLa experiments implicate the distal domain in normal glycosylation without making it necessary for incorporation into the COG complex. This is structural/assembly context, not intrinsic glycosyltransferase activity.

source_access.scope: Complete genuine selected normal abstract read; indexed PMC abstract/Introduction also accessed, but subsequent body retrieval returned a browser challenge. Detailed Methods/Results were not read.
source_access.finding: A recurrent de novo substitution causes Saul-Wilson syndrome with altered fibroblast trafficking and decorin glycosylation, distinct from biallelic COG4 deficiency. The paper reports p.Gly516Arg; these original coordinates are not silently equated to the selected UniProt product.

external_access.scope: Owner read actual selected Methods/Results/Discussion. The separate consultation inspected S7; see its pinned report.

ontology.label: protein-macromolecule adaptor activity
ontology.definition: An adaptor activity that brings together two or more macromolecules in contact, permitting those molecules to function in a coordinated way. The adaptor can bring together two proteins, or a protein and another macromolecule such as a lipid or a nucleic acid.

ontology.label: enzyme binding
ontology.definition: Binding to an enzyme, a protein with catalytic activity.

ontology.label: cytosol
ontology.definition: The part of the cytoplasm that does not contain organelles but which does contain other particulate matter, such as protein complexes.

ontology.label: protein binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a protein.

ontology.label: COG complex
ontology.definition: A multisubunit tethering complex of the CATCHR family (complexes associated with tethering containing helical rods) that has a role in tethering vesicles to the Golgi prior to fusion. Composed of 8 subunits COG1-8.

ontology.label: protein domain specific binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a specific domain of a protein.

ontology.label: helical-bundle zippering fusogenic activity
ontology.definition: Acting as a marker to identify a membrane and interacting selectively with one or more SNAREs on another membrane to mediate membrane fusion.

ontology.label: retrograde vesicle-mediated transport, Golgi to endoplasmic reticulum
ontology.definition: The directed movement of substances from the Golgi back to the endoplasmic reticulum, mediated by vesicles bearing specific protein coats such as COPI or COG.

ontology.label: Golgi membrane
ontology.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments of the Golgi apparatus.

ontology.label: retrograde transport, vesicle recycling within Golgi
ontology.definition: The retrograde movement of substances within the Golgi, mediated by COP I vesicles. Cis-Golgi vesicles are constantly moving forward through the Golgi stack by cisternal progression, eventually becoming trans-Golgi vesicles. They then selectively transport membrane and luminal proteins from the trans- to the medial-Golgi while leaving others behind in the trans-Golgi cisternae; similarly, they selectively move proteins from the medial- to the cis-Golgi.

ontology.label: Golgi organization
ontology.definition: A process that is carried out at the cellular level which results in the assembly, arrangement of constituent parts, or disassembly of the Golgi apparatus.

ontology.label: protein complex scaffold activity
ontology.definition: A structural molecule activity of a protein-containing complex component that serves to hold the complex together. Protein complex scaffolds are integral members of complexes.

ontology.label: trans-Golgi network membrane
ontology.definition: The lipid bilayer surrounding any of the compartments that make up the trans-Golgi network.

ontology.label: ubiquitin protein ligase binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a ubiquitin protein ligase enzyme, any of the E3 proteins.

ontology.label: core promoter sequence-specific DNA binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a sequence of DNA that is part of a core promoter region. The core promoter is composed of the transcription start site and binding sites for the RNA polymerase and the basal transcription machinery. The transcribed region might be described as a gene, cistron, or operon.

ontology.label: syntaxin binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a syntaxin, a SNAP receptor involved in the docking of vesicles.

ontology.label: kinase binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a kinase, any enzyme that catalyzes the transfer of a phosphate group.

ontology.label: cytoskeletal protein binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a protein component of a cytoskeleton (actin, microtubule, or intermediate filament cytoskeleton).

ontology.label: transcription corepressor binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a transcription corepressor, a protein involved in negative regulation of transcription via protein-protein interactions with transcription factors and other proteins that negatively regulate transcription. Transcription corepressors do not bind DNA directly, but rather mediate protein-protein interactions between repressing transcription factors and the basal transcription machinery.

ontology.label: magnesium ion binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a magnesium (Mg) ion.

ontology.label: modification-dependent protein binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a protein upon post-translation modification of the target protein.

ontology.label: cytoskeletal regulatory protein binding
ontology.definition: Binding to a protein involved in modulating the reorganization of the cytoskeleton.
